articles.title: Mumbai-Ahmedabad Bullet Train Gets 2027 Launch Target, Undersea Tunnel Takes Shape
articles.content: Home Breaking News Mumbai-Ahmedabad Bullet Train Gets 2027 Launch Target, Undersea Tunnel Takes Shape Breaking News Mumbai-Ahmedabad Bullet Train Gets 2027 Launch Target, Undersea Tunnel Takes Shape By Harpreet Singh October 26, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp The Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train project is moving towards its first service in the final quarter of 2027, with construction advancing on a 508-kilometre high-speed rail corridor that includes an underground station in Mumbai’s Bandra-Kurla Complex and India’s first undersea rail tunnel beneath Thane Creek. Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw shared the latest project details in a post on X, saying the corridor was no longer only an announcement but a large construction project progressing across Maharashtra, Gujarat and the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli. The first service is planned between Ahmedabad and Mumbai in the final quarter of 2027. The Mumbai terminal is being built at BKC, one of the city’s major business districts. According to the details shared by the minister and reported by Gujarat Samachar, the station is being constructed approximately 32 metres, or around 100 feet, below ground level. The depth is greater than the height of a 10-storey building. The underground station will have three levels for platforms, concourse facilities and services. Six platforms are planned, with each platform measuring more than 400 metres in length. It will be the only underground station on the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail corridor, according to the project update. A few kilometres from the station site, construction is under way on a 7-kilometre rail tunnel beneath Thane Creek. The tunnel is being built by cutting through rock and will carry high-speed trains below the creek. The project update described it as India’s first undersea rail tunnel, making the Mumbai end of the corridor one of its most technically complex sections. The trains are planned to operate at a maximum speed of 320 kilometres per hour, with an average speed of about 300 kilometres per hour between Mumbai and Ahmedabad. The corridor will have 12 main stations: Mumbai BKC, Thane, Virar, Boisar, Vapi, Bilimora, Surat, Bharuch, Vadodara, Anand, Ahmedabad and Sabarmati. The 508-kilometre alignment crosses three administrative regions and includes bridges, tunnels, elevated sections and station structures. The project is being developed as India’s first high-speed rail corridor, with construction activity continuing across the route. The latest update provides the stated launch window and details of the underground and undersea works, but does not provide a revised overall cost, construction completion percentage or a more specific opening date within the final quarter of 2027. The next major milestone identified in the update is the planned start of the first Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train service in the final quarter of 2027, subject to completion of the corridor and associated station, track and tunnel works. articles.title: 4 launch pads by 2029! ISRO reveals a massive space plan with a Gaganyaan surprise
articles.content: Business News LATEST 4 launch pads by 2029! ISRO reveals a massive space plan with a Gaganyaan surprise 4 launch pads by 2029! ISRO reveals a massive space plan with a Gaganyaan surprise ISRO plans four launch pads by 2029, a new Tamil Nadu spaceport and uncrewed Gaganyaan tests. Explore its private-sector push and ambitious Chandrayaan-5 Moon mission with Japan. Business Today Desk Oct 26, 2026, Updated Oct 26, 2026 5:46 PM IST Advertisement Subscribe to Notifications 1/4 Launchpad revolution India's space ambitions are getting a massive upgrade! ISRO Chairman V Narayanan has announced plans to have four functional launch pads by 2029 as the country prepares for a surge in satellite launches. A new 2,000-acre spaceport at Kulasekarapattinam in Tamil Nadu will focus on small satellite missions. But where will the remaining launch pads be located? ISRO has yet to reveal those details. 2/4 Private push Is ISRO going private? Not at all, says its chairman! Narayanan has made it clear that the national space agency will not be privatised. However, private companies and startups will play a much bigger role in India's space ambitions. ISRO plans to transfer technology, support emerging businesses and expand commercial operations, potentially creating thousands of high-tech jobs. 3/4 Gaganyaan countdown India's first human spaceflight mission is approaching another crucial milestone! ISRO plans to conduct its first uncrewed Gaganyaan test within two months of Narayanan's announcement, followed by two more uncrewed missions before astronauts fly. With approximately 8,000 ground experiments already conducted and four astronaut-designates undergoing specialised training, the upcoming tests will put safety and crew escape systems under scrutiny. 4/4 Moon ambition India's next lunar mission could take Moon exploration to another level! ISRO is planning Chandrayaan-5 in collaboration with Japan's space agency, featuring a massive 350-kg rover designed to operate on the lunar surface for 100 days. The ambitious mission aims to conduct extended scientific experiments, showing how India's space programme is looking beyond short-duration lunar exploration. Advertisement

articles.title: Ladakh Becomes India's First Fully Organic Union Territory - GKToday
articles.content: Home Ladakh Becomes India’s First Fully Organic Union Territory Ladakh Becomes India’s First Fully Organic Union Territory October 26, 2026 Current Affairs Today - Latest Current Affairs - 2026-2027 On 25 October 2026, Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena declared Ladakh India’s first 100% organic Union Territory. The declaration followed a phased initiative across Leh and Kargil districts to end the use of synthetic fertilisers, chemical pesticides and toxic soil additives in agriculture. Organic farming standards Organic farming avoids synthetic fertilisers and pesticides and follows standards for production, processing and certification. In India, the National Programme for Organic Production (NPOP) sets standards for organic production and accredits certification bodies. The programme is administered by the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. A tripartite Memorandum of Understanding was signed in July 2021 with the Sikkim State Organic Certification Agency under the Mission Organic Development Initiative. The initiative set a target of making Ladakh a certified organic Union Territory by 2025. Sikkim became India’s first fully organic state in 2016. Agricultural transition in Ladakh In July 2026, the Lieutenant Governor ordered a complete prohibition on the procurement, distribution, sale, marketing and use of chemical and synthetic fertilisers for agriculture across Ladakh. Organic fertiliser consignments were distributed to villages in March 2026, before the sowing season. By 27 July 2026, 207 villages had received organic certification. Of these, 102 villages across Kargil, Dras, Zanskar and Sham were certified on that date. Ladakh’s organic produce includes apricots, sea buckthorn, buckwheat, barley and vegetables. The initiative’s stated objectives include chemical-free farming, environmental conservation and sustainable livelihoods. Certification and implementation Ladakh comprises the districts of Leh and Kargil and is part of the Trans-Himalayan region. Its high-altitude environment includes cold-desert conditions. Farmers had raised concerns about complexities in the NPOP certification process and the cost of imported organic manure. The certification process is distinct from the July 2026 fertiliser prohibition. Important Facts for Exams Sikkim became India’s first fully organic state in 2016. The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority administers the National Programme for Organic Production . Ladakh became a Union Territory on 31 October 2019. The Trans-Himalaya includes high-altitude mountain ranges and plateaux north of the main Himalayan range. Ladakh’s organic certification initiative began under a 2021 agreement with the Sikkim State Organic Certification Agency. The 2026 declaration covered both Leh and Kargil districts. articles.title: Hyundai BAYON Launched IN India - Thrust Zone
articles.content: Home Hyundai Bayon Car News Hyundai Bayon Hyundai BAYON Launched IN India By Mohit Soni 26/10/2026 Follow Us On: Follow Us On: Hyundai Motor India Limited launched the Hyundai BAYON starting at an ex-showroom price of INR 9,99,900. Developed under the philosophy of “Intelligence That Moves,” the vehicle is designed to blend innovation, technology, comfort, and performance. Managing Director and CEO Tarun Garg stated that the launch initiates a new product cycle in India, noting that the SUV will also be exported to over 50 global markets. The vehicle is structured around five pillars: Intelligence On, Safety On, Comfort On, Performance On, and Style On. The Intelligence On feature introduces Hyundai Motor India’s first Generative AI Voice Assistant, utilizing Perplexity intelligence and SoundHound AI voice technology to handle conversational requests regarding travel, weather, news, sports, and local venues. It is equipped with a Connected Car Navigation Cockpit accelerated by NVIDIA, featuring dual 62.5 cm curved panoramic displays, over 70 Hyundai Bluelink connected features, up to 19 controllers for Over-the-Air updates, over 500 embedded voice commands, a multi-language interface supporting 10 regional and 2 international languages, wireless Android Auto and Apple CarPlay, a Bose premium sound system, and a three-year complimentary Bluelink subscription. The body structure incorporates 69% advanced multi-grade high-strength steel using hot stamping, ultra-high-strength steel, advanced high-strength steel, and high-strength steel. The vehicle includes over 80 advanced safety features, such as Hyundai SmartSense Level 2 Pro ADAS with 23 advanced driver assistance capabilities utilizing three radars and 12 parking sensors, Highway Driving Assist, navigation-based smart cruise control zones and curves, a surround view monitor, a blind-spot view monitor, and all-wheel disc brakes. More than 35 safety features are standard across all variants, including six airbags, electronic stability control, hill-start assist control, a rollover sensor, and a high-line tyre pressure monitoring system. A 2,600 mm wheelbase, wider ergonomic seats, front-row ventilated seats, an electric 8-way adjustable driver seat, two-step rear reclining seats, fully automatic temperature control, rear AC vents, a panoramic sunroof, a sliding front console armrest, a rear center armrest with cupholders, a smartphone wireless charger, C-type USB charging ports, a smart key with push-button start, 60:40 split rear seats, and 505 liters of boot space. A four-cylinder 1.5-liter MPi petrol engine that outputs 84.4 kW of maximum power at 6,300 r/min and 143.8 Nm of maximum torque at 4,500 r/min. Transmission options include a 6-speed manual transmission and an Intelligent Variable Transmission. The iVT variant features a Dash Boost Mode and Sporty Drive Tech, complemented by selectable drive modes including Eco, Normal, and Sport with a steering-mounted button, paddle shifters, and Idle Stop & Go. The exterior styling features an upright stance, a sculpted bonnet design, H-edge LED DRLs, high-intensity dual LED projector headlamps, geometric wheel arches, wrap-around door cladding, bridge-type roof rails, R17 diamond-cut alloy wheels, H-edge LED tail lamps, and a sporty spoiler with a vertical aerolight high-mounted stop lamp.
